keyFigures.name: Jeffrey Epstein
keyFigures.detail: Sex trafficker who abused dozens of minors over decades. Died in federal custody on August 10, 2019. His death was ruled a suicide, though many dispute the official findings.

keyFigures.name: Ghislaine Maxwell
keyFigures.detail: Convicted in December 2021 on five federal counts including sex trafficking of minors. Sentenced to 20 years in federal prison. Currently serving her sentence.

keyFigures.name: Prince Andrew
keyFigures.detail: Duke of York. Stepped down from royal duties in November 2019 following his disastrous BBC interview about Epstein. Settled a civil lawsuit with Virginia Giuffre in 2022 for an undisclosed sum.

keyFigures.name: Alexander Acosta
keyFigures.detail: As U.S. Attorney for Southern Florida, Acosta negotiated Epstein's controversial 2008 plea deal, which critics called a sweetheart deal. Resigned as Labor Secretary in July 2019 following public outcry.

keyFigures.name: Les Wexner
keyFigures.detail: Founder of L Brands and Victoria's Secret. Gave Epstein sweeping power of attorney and transferred his Manhattan mansion to him. Has denied knowledge of Epstein's crimes.

keyFigures.name: Virginia Giuffre
keyFigures.detail: One of Epstein's most prominent survivors. Filed lawsuits against Maxwell, Prince Andrew, and others. Her testimony was central to Maxwell's conviction. Has advocated tirelessly for other victims.

keyFigures.name: Alan Dershowitz
keyFigures.detail: Part of Epstein's legal team that negotiated the 2008 plea deal. Named in civil lawsuits by accusers including Virginia Giuffre. Has denied all allegations against him.

keyFigures.name: Bill Barr
keyFigures.detail: Oversaw the Department of Justice during Epstein's arrest and subsequent death in 2019. His father Donald Barr hired Epstein to teach at the Dalton School in the 1970s despite Epstein lacking a degree.

keyFigures.name: Bill Clinton
keyFigures.detail: Flew on Epstein's private jet multiple times according to flight logs. His office has denied any knowledge of Epstein's crimes.

keyFigures.name: Woody Allen
keyFigures.detail: Regular guest at Epstein's Upper East Side townhouse from 2010 onward. Wrote a letter for Epstein's 63rd birthday. Photographed with Epstein on a private plane alongside Larry Summers.

keyFigures.name: Anil Ambani
keyFigures.detail: Introduced to Epstein by Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem while seeking White House connections. Visited Epstein's Manhattan townhouse the day Modi secured re-election in 2019.

keyFigures.name: Eva Andersson-Dubin
keyFigures.detail: Epstein's girlfriend for 11 years before marrying Glenn Dubin. The Dubins flew on Epstein's planes at least 18 times between 1996 and 2005.

keyFigures.name: Dan Ariely
keyFigures.detail: Had a longstanding relationship with Epstein. In a 2012 email asked Epstein for the name and email of a woman he had met earlier.

keyFigures.name: Peter Attia
keyFigures.detail: His name appeared over 1,700 times in the files. Told Epstein: 'the life you lead is so outrageous, and yet I can't tell a soul.' Lost several professional positions following revelations.

keyFigures.name: Richard Axel
keyFigures.detail: Met Epstein in the 1980s and corresponded until shortly before Epstein's death. He and his wife were invited to Epstein's island multiple times. Stepped down from the Zuckerman Mind Brain Behavior Institute.

keyFigures.name: Jose Maria Aznar
keyFigures.detail: Listed in the files as a recipient of two parcels from Epstein in 2003 and 2004. Contents were not specified.

keyFigures.name: Joscha Bach
keyFigures.detail: MIT Media Lab researcher whose work was subsidized by Epstein. Wrote racist and sexist views to Epstein in 2016.

keyFigures.name: Doug Band
keyFigures.detail: Connected Bill Clinton to Epstein. Flew on Epstein's private jet more than 35 times. Maxwell and Epstein gifted Band a $35,000 Audemars Piguet watch in 2005.

keyFigures.name: Steve Bannon
keyFigures.detail: Exchanged thousands of texts with Epstein to discuss influencing European coalitions, pressuring China, and forging Middle East ties. Epstein lent him his Paris apartment, Palm Beach house, and plane.

keyFigures.name: Ehud Barak
keyFigures.detail: Exchanged emails with Epstein about Federal Reserve politics. Epstein nudged Barak to work with Thiel's Palantir. Frequented a Manhattan building managed by Epstein for extended stays.

keyFigures.name: Tom Barrack
keyFigures.detail: Friends with Epstein and Trump among New York elite in the 1980s-1990s. Had business ties to the Middle East with Epstein by early 2000s.

keyFigures.name: Sergei Belyakov
keyFigures.detail: Epstein emailed Belyakov about a Russian girl attempting to blackmail businessmen in New York.

keyFigures.name: Leon Black
keyFigures.detail: Epstein referred to as 'Mr. Big.' Paid Epstein $170 million for tax advice. JPMorgan filed a suspicious activity report for Black's transactions totalling about $1 billion. Stepped down from Apollo Global Management.

keyFigures.name: David Blaine
keyFigures.detail: Files showed years-long correspondence with Epstein and regular dinners between 2012 and 2016. Agreed to write a letter of support for an unidentified woman's U.S. visa application in 2015.

keyFigures.name: Todd Boehly
keyFigures.detail: Emails from 2011 showed Epstein arranged two meetings with Boehly, then a managing partner at Guggenheim Partners.

keyFigures.name: Leon Botstein
keyFigures.detail: Met Epstein numerous times after his 2008 conviction, soliciting donations. Received $150,000 from Epstein in 2016.

keyFigures.name: Edward Boyden
keyFigures.detail: Attended a 2015 Silicon Valley dinner hosted by Reid Hoffman where Epstein also photographed himself with Musk, Thiel, and Zuckerberg.

keyFigures.name: Richard Branson
keyFigures.detail: 2013 email exchange with Epstein suggested a familiar relationship. Branson wrote: 'Any time you're in the area would love to see you. As long as you bring your harem!'

keyFigures.name: Borge Brende
keyFigures.detail: Exchanged more than 120 emails and texts with Epstein. Was a guest at several dinners at Epstein's NYC townhouse.

keyFigures.name: Flavio Briatore
keyFigures.detail: Maintained email contact with Epstein, who referred to him as his 'Italian friend' in a 2010 email.

keyFigures.name: Sergey Brin
keyFigures.detail: Contacted Ghislaine Maxwell about attending dinners at Epstein's home.

keyFigures.name: John Brockman
keyFigures.detail: Epstein was the biggest donor to Brockman's Edge Foundation. Epstein funded numerous private dinners attended by Silicon Valley billionaires. In 2018 Epstein advised Brockman not to care about diversity.

keyFigures.name: David Brooks
keyFigures.detail: Appears in several photos in the files from a 2011 event with Epstein. Later wrote a 2025 New York Times column dismissing continuing media coverage of Epstein.

keyFigures.name: Jean-Luc Brunel
keyFigures.detail: Founded MC2 Model Management with Epstein's financing. Listed as passenger on Epstein's plane 25 times between 1998-2005. Visited Epstein in jail at least 70 times in 2008. Died in prison in 2022.

keyFigures.name: William Burns
keyFigures.detail: Had three meetings with Epstein in 2014 when Burns was deputy secretary of state. CIA stated Epstein was introduced as a financial sector expert offering private sector advice.

keyFigures.name: Naomi Campbell
keyFigures.detail: Frequently invited Epstein to lavish events worldwide. Epstein used his association with her to convince people he could help them start modeling careers or get jobs at Victoria's Secret.

keyFigures.name: Nick Candy
keyFigures.detail: Appears in emails from 2004 meeting Epstein associates. In 2010 offered a Knightsbridge property to Epstein for 80 million pounds. Epstein said 'I like both of those guys' about Nick and his brother Christian.

keyFigures.name: Frederic Chaslin
keyFigures.detail: In a 2013 email wrote to Epstein that he had 'found a great girl for your next stay in Paris. Philosophy student. 21.'

keyFigures.name: Noam Chomsky
keyFigures.detail: Met with Epstein multiple times after his conviction. Attended dinners at Epstein's Manhattan townhouse.

keyFigures.name: Bill Clinton
keyFigures.detail: Flew on Epstein's private jet multiple times according to flight logs. His office has denied any knowledge of Epstein's crimes.

keyFigures.name: Hillary Clinton
keyFigures.detail: Named in Epstein files in connection with her husband's association with Epstein. Her office has denied any wrongdoing.

keyFigures.name: Glenn Dubin
keyFigures.detail: Married Eva Andersson, Epstein's former girlfriend. The Dubins flew on Epstein's planes at least 18 times between 1996 and 2005. JPMorgan filed suspicious activity reports for Dubin's transactions.

keyFigures.name: Alan Dershowitz
keyFigures.detail: Part of Epstein's legal team that negotiated the controversial 2008 plea deal. Named in civil lawsuits by accusers including Virginia Giuffre. Has denied all allegations.

keyFigures.name: Alexander Acosta
keyFigures.detail: As U.S. Attorney for Southern Florida, negotiated Epstein's controversial 2008 plea deal. Resigned as Labor Secretary in July 2019 following public outcry.

keyFigures.name: Jeffrey Epstein
keyFigures.detail: Convicted sex offender who abused dozens of minors over decades. Built a vast network of powerful associates. Died in federal custody on August 10, 2019.

keyFigures.name: Ghislaine Maxwell
keyFigures.detail: Convicted in December 2021 on five federal counts including sex trafficking of minors. Sentenced to 20 years in federal prison. Currently serving her sentence.

keyFigures.name: Prince Andrew
keyFigures.detail: Stepped down from royal duties in November 2019 following his BBC interview. Settled a civil lawsuit with Virginia Giuffre in 2022 for an undisclosed sum.

keyFigures.name: Bill Barr
keyFigures.detail: Oversaw the DOJ during Epstein's arrest and death in 2019. His father Donald Barr hired Epstein to teach at the Dalton School in the 1970s despite Epstein lacking a degree.

keyFigures.name: Les Wexner
keyFigures.detail: Gave Epstein sweeping power of attorney and transferred his Manhattan mansion to him. Paid Epstein tens of millions. Has denied knowledge of Epstein's crimes.

keyFigures.name: Virginia Giuffre
keyFigures.detail: One of Epstein's most prominent survivors. Filed lawsuits against Maxwell, Prince Andrew, and others. Her testimony was central to Maxwell's conviction.

keyFigures.name: Reid Hoffman
keyFigures.detail: Hosted a 2015 dinner in Palo Alto attended by Epstein, Musk, Thiel, and Zuckerberg. Has acknowledged meeting Epstein but denied close ties.

keyFigures.name: Elon Musk
keyFigures.detail: Photographed at a 2015 Silicon Valley dinner hosted by Reid Hoffman alongside Epstein. Has stated he never met Epstein and was unaware of his presence at the dinner.

keyFigures.name: Peter Thiel
keyFigures.detail: Photographed at a 2015 dinner with Epstein. Epstein nudged Ehud Barak to work with Thiel's Palantir in a 2013 recording.

keyFigures.name: Mark Zuckerberg
keyFigures.detail: Photographed at a 2015 Silicon Valley dinner hosted by Reid Hoffman where Epstein was also present.

keyFigures.name: Larry Summers
keyFigures.detail: Photographed on a private plane alongside Epstein and Woody Allen. Named in emails discussing Federal Reserve chair candidacy.

keyFigures.name: Henry Kissinger
keyFigures.detail: Referenced in Epstein's emails. Epstein scheduled Ehud Barak to meet a 'Kissinger China guy' in a 2013 email chain.

keyFigures.name: Ariane de Rothschild
keyFigures.detail: Epstein arranged for Ehud Barak to meet with her in 2013.

keyFigures.name: Tom Pritzker
keyFigures.detail: Received an email from Epstein describing a 2015 Silicon Valley dinner as 'wild.'

keyFigures.name: Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem
keyFigures.detail: Introduced Anil Ambani to Epstein.

keyFigures.name: Terje Rod-Larsen
keyFigures.detail: Introduced Borge Brende to Epstein. Photographed at Epstein's New York home with Bannon and Brende.

keyFigures.name: Ari Emanuel
keyFigures.detail: Named in Epstein files. Attended events connected to Epstein's network.

keyFigures.name: Marvin Minsky
keyFigures.detail: Received funding from Epstein for his MIT Media Lab research. Named in Virginia Giuffre's allegations.

keyFigures.name: Lawrence Krauss
keyFigures.detail: Had a years-long friendship with Epstein, who donated to his academic work. Resigned from Arizona State University following misconduct allegations.

keyFigures.name: Stephen Hawking
keyFigures.detail: Attended a conference on Epstein's private island in 2006, one year after Epstein's first arrest.

keyFigures.name: Sarah Kellen
keyFigures.detail: One of Epstein's closest associates and alleged co-conspirators. Managed logistics for Epstein's activities.

keyFigures.name: Nadia Marcinkova
keyFigures.detail: Alleged co-conspirator and Epstein associate. Named in multiple victim testimonies.

keyFigures.name: Lesley Groff
keyFigures.detail: Long-time executive assistant to Epstein. Named as an alleged co-conspirator in court documents.
